The famous ship that sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg is the **RMS Titanic**.

To explain the complex concept of blockchain technology using an analogy, imagine a massive, shared notebook that is kept by a huge community rather than a single bank or company.

1.  **The Decentralized Ledger**: Instead of one person holding the only copy of this notebook, thousands of people around the world each have an identical copy. This is what "decentralized" means—no single point of failure or control.
2.  **Immutability**: Once a page is filled with transactions and sealed, it cannot be erased or rewritten. If you try to change a past entry in your copy, it won't match the thousands of other copies.
3.  **Verification and Consensus**: If someone tries to add a new, fraudulent entry to their notebook, the other thousands of people will check their own copies. Since the majority of the network agrees on what the true history is, they will reject the fake entry. This "majority agreement" process ensures that the data remains secure and trustworthy, as it is nearly impossible for a hacker to alter the record without controlling more than half of all the computers in the network.
